By the early 20th century, the Chinese city of Tianjin held concessions belonging to eight different foreign powers — plus a ninth, American one already folded into Britain's. No other city in China hosted more.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ It started with defeat. The 1860 Convention of Peking, forced on China after the Second Opium War, opened Tianjin to British and French settlement — the first two concessions on this map, both dated 1860.
2/ Six more followed by 1902: Germany, Japan, Russia, Belgium, Italy, and Austria-Hungary each carved out their own walled district, with its own police, courts, and street signs in its own language.
3/ Germany and Austria-Hungary lost theirs first — not through negotiation but because China declared war on the Central Powers in 1917 and simply reclaimed both concessions on the spot.
4/ Russia's concession unraveled by 1920, as the old imperial consulate lost any authority to defend it amid the Russian Civil War. Belgium handed its concession back peacefully in 1931.

5/ Japan's concession, established in 1888, ran the longest of the original powers and ended only with Japan's 1945 surrender. Italy's technically outlasted everyone — seized by Japan in 1943 after Italy switched sides, not returned to China until 1947.

6/ By 1947 the age of foreign concessions in Tianjin was over. What's left are the street grids on this map — each one still recognizably following the layout its original foreign occupant designed.
